findings.text: follow-on: the fragment's method sentence, and the manifest's evidence_inputs, double-count PSRC Ip. The fragment lists the channel list as 'magnetics (44 MDAC flux loops and probes + PSRC Ip), pf_active (10 MMSYS coil currents) and tf (MMSYS cur1TFLKAT)' plus 'the 48 single-channel PSRC equilibrium arrays' plus FAME/VOLUM and FAME/BETA, then states '105 channels per shot'. Those named items sum to 44+1+10+1+48+2 = 106, not 105: PSRC/Ip is source-array ('PSRC','Ip') in the magnetics map (imas_ambix/data/maps/jt-60sa/magnetics.json signals) AND the second entry of the 48-array _PSRC_EQUILIBRIUM list in the run's fetch_op1.py, so the (source_group, source_array) set that fetch_op1.py builds deduplicates it to one. The served/refused totals (105 per full shot, 1678 overall) are correct and independently reproduced; only the decomposition is internally inconsistent, so a reader who adds the parenthesised items gets 106. The fix is to state that PSRC/Ip is one of the 48 equilibrium arrays rather than an extra magnetics channel.

follow-on: the manifest's tests line is not the command that ran - it carries two unsubstituted angle-bracket placeholders, 'PYTHONPATH=<worktree>:<worktree>/packages/imas-alambic/src /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-ambix/.venv/bin/python fetch_op1.py 0 16'. The gate field must be the literal command with absolute paths, so a later reader cannot re-run it as written. The run's own log (fetch_op1.log) shows the result (16 shots, 1678 served, 2 refused, 16 ssh sessions), and the script fetch_op1.py is in the run directory, so the intended command is recoverable - but the manifest field itself is a template.

follow_ons.text: The caching driver fetch_op1.py lives only in the store's own run directory, not in the repository, so the node's own caching step is not reproducible from the repo tree; the durable artifact is the populated /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa cache and the per-shot evidence fragment, both of which are sufficient for the plan's next nodes. Recorded so the caching step is not read as an in-repo entry point.

The measure is met.

At head 27afa17d the fragment reports that all 16 shots in jtmm-op1-shot-survey.json were cached, one fetch_channels call each (one RemoteEddbExtractor batch, one ssh session via DEFAULT_SSH_COMMAND = ssh -F ~/.ssh/config jt-60sa), covering the served source arrays of the JT-60SA magnetics (44 MDAC + PSRC Ip), pf_active (10 MMSYS) and tf (1 MMSYS) signal maps, the single-channel PSRC equilibrium arrays, and FAME VOLUM/BETA - 105 unique channels per shot - with PSRC included on all 16 (psrc_present true for every shot). The clause is met.

justifications.durability: The populated /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa stores and the per-shot evidence fragment are durable and self-describing, and the fragments's numbers reproduce from the run's logs; held below full because the caching driver fetch_op1.py lives only in the run directory rather than the repository, so the caching step cannot be re-run from the repo tree, and the fragment does not cite the fetch_op1_progress.json raw record path in its own text (only the manifest does).
justifications.evidence: Every headline number reproduces from the run's own artifacts and from the store: the 16 rows match fetch_op1.log; 15x105+103=1678 served and 2 refused reproduce; 2245.8 MB is the exact byte sum of the 16 .zarr trees (2245824478 B); the survey corroborates 16 shots and fame_present false only for E100599; and I verified from source that one fetch_batch is one transport.run (eddb_remote.py:377) and that second-read requests are short-circuited in fetch_channels before any transport call (eddb.py:349-355). I also ran an independent mutation (review_secondread_probe.log): an all-cached request returned 0 records/0 refusals/0 transport calls, while an uncached request raised through the transport (1 call), so the no-transport second read is a live, falsifiable signal and not a vacuous zero. Held below full because the fragment reads that 0-record result as proof the warm read is 'served wholly from disk', which fetch_channels does not measure - it returns an empty BatchResult for fully-cached requests without reading the store, so the check evidences the short-circuit, not store readability; a read_channel on one cached channel would evidence that.
justifications.fit: The fragment carries the class="evidence-fragment" data-reckon="evidence" wrapper, every element id is prefixed with the node id (jtmm-op1-shot-fetch-landing/-h/-method/-table/-totals/-controls/-gate), and the table carries a unit column (wall [s]); it writes no figure, which is correct because the node's done-when names no figure and the contract forbids prose/figure beyond the named artifact.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node does its clause completely - all 16 listed shots cached with PSRC, one ssh each, nothing refetched - and the fragment reports the required per-shot served/refused with codes; held one point below full because the deliverable's own method sentence decomposes the 105 channels as 106 items by double-counting PSRC/Ip (it is both a magnetics map source array and one of the 48 equilibrium arrays), so the description of what was fetched is internally inconsistent even though the totals are right.
justifications.reuse: Additive and read-only with respect to source: the node adds no module, reader, binding or abstraction in the repository and reuses the existing fetch_channels/is_cached/RemoteEddbExtractor path; it retires nothing, so the reuse budget is clean.
justifications.scope_discipline: The single commit 27afa17d touches exactly the one declared fragment path and nothing else (git show --stat: 1 file, +27); no plan, sprint, index, test or other node's file is modified, and the data writes land in the shared cache the plan names.
